changes.summary: Drizzle collections support explicit refetch mode for metadata-only Postgres revision feeds and projected rows

changes.detail: The optional `@absolutejs/isolated-jsc` peer range is now `>=0.12.2 <1.0.0`, so a new isolated-jsc minor no longer needs a sync release before apps can install it. Sync uses only isolated-jsc's stable sandbox APIs (`resolveIsolatePolicy`, the isolated runner), and its sandbox tests run against each isolated-jsc release it is bumped to; this one is tested with 0.15.0.
changes.summary: Sandboxed handlers accept any isolated-jsc 0.x from 0.12.2

changes.detail: The optional `@absolutejs/isolated-jsc` peer range now allows 0.14. With 0.14, the `cpuMs` that sandboxed-handler metrics report is the isolate thread's CPU time instead of the wall-clock duration, so a handler waiting on a host call is no longer charged for the wait.

Sandboxed mutation handlers take `requireLockdown`, passed through to isolated-jsc 0.13+. On the Worker backend, stock Bun lets a handler reach the `Bun` global through indirect eval and load any module with `import()`; AbsoluteJS patched Bun 1.4.4+absolute.2 closes both with `lockdown()`. With `requireLockdown: true`, the handler refuses to run on a Worker isolate that is not locked down and throws `LockdownUnavailableError` instead. Default `false`, so nothing changes unless you set it. The `@absolutejs/isolated-jsc` peer range now allows 0.13; older versions ignore the option.
changes.summary: Sandboxed handlers can require a locked-down isolate
Bound pending authentication queues and retire timed-out sockets before late context resolution
Read WebSocket buffer usage from the underlying Elysia transport and allow queued temporary backpressure to drain without reconnecting; enforce configured byte limits independently of notifications
Release late subscriptions after connection close or unsubscribe, reject duplicate in-flight subscription IDs, and prevent sends after close

changes.detail: Elysia 2.0.0-rc.0 renamed every lifecycle hook to its `on` form and removed `setup`/`cleanup`. sync's peer ranges (`elysia ^2.0.0-beta.6`, `@elysia/cron ^2.0.0-beta.1`) accepted it untested. sync now builds and tests against Elysia 2.0.0-rc.0 and requires `^2.0.0-rc.0` for both; the plugins whose types carry Elysia's are listed below. No sync API changed shape.

migration.instruction: Upgrade `elysia` and every `@elysia/*` package (including `@elysia/cron`) to 2.0.0-rc.0 or later 2.x, then rename lifecycle hooks in your app: request → onRequest, beforeHandle → onBeforeHandle, afterHandle → onAfterHandle, afterResponse → onAfterResponse, error → onError, parse → onParse, transform → onTransform; setup/cleanup → onStart/onStop.

changes.summary: Server reactions without timers: createPostgresSignalReaction (from @absolutejs/sync/postgres) runs durable work on NOTIFY and catches up on (re)connect; the table revision source accepts reconcileMs: false
Serve more than one syncSocket in an app: each socket plugin is seeded by its path, so Elysia no longer drops the second as a duplicate
Support schema-qualified PostgreSQL revision feeds without colliding subscription keys
Republish socket authentication fix after npm served metadata but returned 404 for the 2.32.1 tarball
Close rejected or stalled socket context authentication without leaking internal errors
Postgres transactional mutation receipts and payload-free committed table revision source
